briefs.headline: Parkersburg Catholic beats Hannan 7-2 at Ashton, MaxPreps posts
briefs.summary: MaxPreps lists Tuesday's home match as a 7-2 loss to the Crusaders, the first result it has posted for Hannan since Aug. 27, and puts the record at 1-2; the Sept. 9 Point Pleasant JV and Sept. 10 Westside matches no longer appear on its schedule at all. Hannan plays at Westside on Thursday at 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round
briefs.summary: Alexis Mac Allister curled in from the edge of the area in the 21st minute and Cody Gakpo drove across goal early in the second half; Conor Gallagher headed in a corner with 21 minutes left before Dominik Szoboszlai struck from 25 yards in stoppage time. Andoni Iraola made 10 changes before a crowd of 60,169; the fourth-round draw is Wednesday.

briefs.headline: De Zerbi says Tottenham 'need a click' after the 3-1 loss at Anfield
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi said Tottenham "created chances to win the game" and that "there are many positives" after Tuesday's Carabao Cup exit; Conor Gallagher's header was the club's first goal against top-flight opposition this season. Giorgi Mamardashvili denied Lucas Bergvall and Omar Marmoush. Aston Villa visits Saturday at 7:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Yamamoto one-hits the Reds over seven innings as the Dodgers win 4-0
briefs.summary: Yoshinobu Yamamoto allowed one hit, walked two and struck out seven in 91 pitches Tuesday at Great American Ball Park; Teoscar Hernandez's two-run homer off Rhett Lowder built the lead and Alex Freeland homered in the seventh. Cincinnati had three hits, Lowder allowed three runs in five innings, and Los Angeles has won nine straight against the Reds.

briefs.headline: Browns put Dylan Sampson on injured reserve and sign Jaleel McLaughlin
briefs.summary: The second-year running back hurt a knee in the opener at Jacksonville, the team said Tuesday; McLaughlin, who ran for 1,093 yards in 41 games with Denver, moves up from the practice squad. The Week 2 depth chart lists Deshaun Watson first at quarterback and Teven Jenkins at right guard for Sunday at Tampa Bay.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati waives Matt Miazga and loans Stiven Jimenez to Fluminense
briefs.summary: The club bought out the 2023 MLS Defender of the Year's guaranteed contract, retroactive to Sept. 2, after 108 appearances since 2022; general manager Chris Albright said Monday the club was "tremendously grateful for all that Matt did." Jimenez, 19, the youngest signing in club history, goes to Brazil through December after three appearances this season.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Pirates 5-1 and clinch a fourth straight NL Central title
briefs.summary: Jacob Misiorowski struck out seven over five innings of singles at PNC Park on Tuesday, and Milwaukee scored four in the sixth after Lake Bachar lasted two innings; Brandon Lowe's eighth-inning homer, his 30th, was Pittsburgh's run on 10 hits. The clinch came about 50 minutes after the final out, when the Cubs lost to Atlanta.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says Talley is out a week or two and a Thomas hearing moves to Thursday
briefs.summary: Rich Rodriguez said Tuesday running back Chris Talley may need one or two more weeks and that Georgia transfer JaCorey Thomas' hearing has moved to Thursday, when the team may learn his status. The two-deep is unchanged for Saturday's game against No. 25 Virginia, which he called "one of the most veteran teams in the country."

briefs.headline: Takayasu beats yokozuna Onosato and leaves Kotozakura the last unbeaten man
briefs.summary: Maegashira Takayasu, 36, thrust down the yokozuna (grand champion) by tsukitaoshi (thrust-down) at Ryogoku Kokugikan on Wednesday for his seventh kinboshi (gold star); Onosato has three wins and one loss. Ozeki (champion) Kotozakura threw Gonoyama and is the only top-division man at four wins and no losses.

briefs.headline: Aonishiki loses to winless Hakunofuji while Kirishima and Atamifuji win
briefs.summary: New komusubi (fourth rank) Hakunofuji pushed out the ozeki (champion) for his first win in seven meetings and his first of the tournament; Aonishiki is three wins and one loss. Kirishima, chasing yokozuna (grand champion) rank, forced out Kotoeimine, and sekiwake (junior champion) Atamifuji pushed down Fujiryoga; both are three and one.

briefs.headline: Onosato draws winless Yoshinofuji on Day 5 and Kotozakura meets Mitoumi
briefs.summary: Thursday's card in Tokyo, ending early Thursday ET, sends the yokozuna (grand champion) against Yoshinofuji, winless in four bouts; Aonishiki faces Gonoyama, Kirishima draws Takanosho and Atamifuji meets komusubi (fourth rank) Daieisho. Sekiwake (junior champion) Fujinokawa was pushed out by Kotoshoho and is two and two.

briefs.headline: Guardians walk off the White Sox 7-6 and pull within a half-game in the AL Central
briefs.summary: Brayan Rocchio's two-out, two-run double in the ninth off Grant Taylor finished a comeback from 6-5 down Tuesday; Travis Bazzana homered twice and Jo Adell once. Chicago leads Cleveland by a half-game with 11 games left, and Cleveland holds the AL's last wild card, 1.5 games ahead of Texas.

briefs.headline: Braves beat the Cubs 6-3 and hand Milwaukee the NL Central title
briefs.summary: Ronald Acuna Jr., Ozzie Albies and Drake Baldwin hit two-run homers from the sixth inning on at Wrigley Field on Tuesday, and the result clinched the division for Milwaukee. Washington beat Philadelphia 6-3 and Colorado beat San Diego 9-3; Chicago still leads the wild card by a half-game.

briefs.headline: Caminero's 41st homer ends it in the ninth as the Rays beat the Athletics 2-1
briefs.summary: Junior Caminero's leadoff homer off Elvis Alvarado on Tuesday was his second game-ending home run in four games; Tampa Bay, already in the playoffs, has won four straight and leads the Yankees by 3.5 in the AL East. New York beat Minnesota 8-1 behind seven innings from Max Fried.

briefs.headline: Dowman, 16, scores twice as Arsenal beat Ipswich 4-2 in the Carabao Cup
briefs.summary: Max Dowman scored in the seventh and 47th minutes at Portman Road on Tuesday in his first appearance of the season; Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino also scored for a side showing nine changes, and Anis Mehmeti and Chuba Akpom replied. "We need to look after him," Mikel Arteta said.

briefs.headline: Fulham beat West Ham 3-2 as Peterborough go through on penalties
briefs.summary: Substitute Oscar Bobb's 78th-minute goal, his first for the club, settled the tie at London Stadium after Rodrigo Muniz and Cesar Palacios put Fulham ahead and Morato and Pablo twice leveled. Peterborough beat Barnsley 7-6 on penalties after a 3-3 draw and Brentford won 2-1 at Reading; Manchester United host Brighton on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Vanderbilt names freshman Jared Curtis its starting quarterback for NC State
briefs.summary: Coach Clark Lea said Tuesday that Curtis, a five-star recruit and the highest-rated signee in program history, replaces Blaze Berlowitz for Saturday's game. Curtis went 14 of 22 for 210 yards with a passing touchdown and two rushing scores against Delaware; Vanderbilt has won both of its games. "He's earned it," Lea said.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Three days out. The migratory bird summary, downloaded and read again this morning, lists Saturday, Sept. 19, and Oct. 31 as the two single youth waterfowl days for ducks, geese, coots, gallinules and mergansers, open to hunters under 18; footnote (b) sets the youth-day bag at the daily limit of the regular duck and goose seasons, except that two scaup may be taken as part of the six-duck daily bag. Hunters under 15 must be accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older who may not hunt or carry a firearm, only nontoxic shot size T or smaller may be carried, shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and every licensed hunter needs a HIP registration card. The same table opens the regular duck season Oct. 3-11 at six a day and 18 in possession.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Three days out. The second gun window for bear runs Saturday, Sept. 19, through Sept. 25 in SELECTED COUNTIES, a list the summary table does not carry, so no county is named here; the county-by-county rules and limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class. Electronic registration is required. The next gun windows are Oct. 3-9 and Oct. 22-25.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Ten days out. Archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear both open Saturday, Sept. 26, and run through Dec. 31, with electronic registration required for each; the deer and bear bag limits are not in the summary table at all, only on pamphlet pages 13-18 and 33-39, and are not printed here. Wild boar archery and crossbow opens the same day, one a season.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: Seventeen days out. The migratory bird summary's next goose date is Oct. 3, the first of three splits, five a day and 15 in possession in aggregate under footnote (d), with snow and blue geese on the same dates. Shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. At McClintic and Green Bottom wildlife management areas, waterfowl hours run only until noon Oct. 3-11, and the McClintic controlled area is by permit in that window.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: Day 5. The general squirrel season opened Saturday, Sept. 12, and runs through Feb. 28, and the summary table sets the daily bag at six and the possession limit at 24, with no season limit and no registration requirement.
prime.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: The first dove segment is in its 16th day with 25 days left after today, running through Oct. 11, with a daily bag of 15 and a possession limit of 45, per the migratory bird summary read again this morning; shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset for the rest of the segment, and HIP registration is required. Sora and Virginia rails run Sept. 1 to Nov. 9, 10 a day and 30 in possession in aggregate, and Wilson's snipe Sept. 1 to Dec. 16, eight and 24, on the same table.
prime.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries recreational limits page, effective Sept. 2 and opened again this morning, holds red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one a day, with footnote C making a drum over 27 inches unlawful to possess and barring gigs, spears and gaffs. In the Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 15 days old, Native Son had the drum bite steady at docks and creek mouths on topwater early and slower, deeper presentations or natural bait as the sun rose, Speckled Specialist had reds in small groups around oysters, docks, grass points and ledges, Carolina Flats had the action in the morning on topwater, and Spring Tide reported over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches moving in and not staying put.

Limits page: 14 to 20 inches total length, three a day, one of the three allowed over 26 inches. Speckled Specialist's Sept. 1 paragraph in the Fisherman's Post says trout numbers vary trip to trip but the quality is strong, East Coast Sports had them with the drum around structure and grass banks early and late, Surf City Pier had them early and in the evening, and Native Son called them occasional; a 15-day-old monthly report, not this morning's water.

Limits page: Spanish 12-inch fork length, 15 a day; bluefish no minimum, and footnote M sets the creel at three per person per day in private recreational fishing and five aboard a for-hire vessel. East Coast Sports' Sept. 1 paragraph had both on casting jigs from the surf and piers with the early bite best, Jolly Roger Pier called them hit-or-miss on plugs early and late, Surf City Pier had Spanish on Gotcha plugs, and Native Son was seeing a better class of Spanish over 3 pounds off the beach, 15 days ago.

Limits page: black drum 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 a day, with footnote C allowing one of them over 25 inches; sheepshead 14 inches total length, five a day. The Fisherman's Post Sept. 1 report, 15 days old, has black drum in the bottom fishing at both Jolly Roger and Surf City piers and does not mention sheepshead this month.

sections.note: Nothing on either state's calendar closes within two weeks: North Carolina's recreational flounder harvest ended Sept. 14 and the Marine Fisheries limits page, opened this morning, still prints 'Sep 15-30: CLOSED, unlawful to possess', so it comes off the list; West Virginia's early Canada goose season closed Sept. 13 and the first dove segment has 25 days to run. The second Gauley release window opens Friday, Sept. 18, and runs through Monday, Sept. 21, two days out: the National Park Service's whitewater page for the Gauley River answered this morning and lists the Corps of Engineers' planned Summersville Lake releases as Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18. Gauley Fest opens Thursday, Sept. 17, and runs through Sunday, Sept. 20, at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville, per American Whitewater's event page, which gives 8 a.m. Thursday to noon Sunday; the Eventbrite listing gives different hours, so no hours are printed. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, carries nothing new: the Sept. 14 Forest Road 19 Dolly Sods closure, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 closure on the Gauley district, the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground bridge alert and the July Forest Road 86-Williams River closure stand. A search for WVDNR trout stocking in September 2026 found no notice, the division's stocking page lists no September entry, and its fall-stocking page still carries the 2025 article, so nothing is printed. The WV hunting reference file is valid through June 30, 2027, and was checked against today's date.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.reading: 72.9 cfs, 1.47 feet, falling, three days off the Sunday-evening crest.
waters.working: Down 33 cfs from the 106.0 this paper printed at this hour Tuesday, and the recession is nearly flat: the USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:37 a.m., runs from 186 cfs and 2.03 feet at 5:45 a.m. Monday through 105 at 5:45 a.m. Tuesday, 93.8 at 11:45, 87.0 at 5:45 p.m., 82.1 at 9:45, 77.4 at 1:45 a.m., 74.4 from 3:45 to 4:45 and 72.9 at 5 and 5:15 this morning, about 1.3 cfs an hour now against three yesterday. The fetcher's falling flag compares against Monday morning's 186.0 and 2.03, the first point of the two-day trace, and happens to agree with the trace. At 72.9 cfs and 1.47 feet the river is 17 cfs and a tenth of a foot over the 56.2 cfs and 1.35 feet this paper printed for Sunday morning before the rain, and the pockets are readable again, so this is back to the long-leader, small-fly problem: caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage, and pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the structure, which at this flow means a 12-foot leader tapered to 6X, a size 16 to 18 caddis dry or elk-hair emerger fished up through the pocket heads and the tailouts of the plunge pools, a size 16 stonefly nymph or pheasant tail dropped a foot under it in the deeper seams, and a small olive sculpin swung tight under the undercut banks before the sun is on the water, because at this height every fish in the pockets can see a shadow. NWS Charleston's forecast for Cowen is sunny with a high near 84 and a southwest wind around 3, partly cloudy and 63 tonight; Thursday brings showers and thunderstorms likely between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. at a 60% chance with a tenth to a quarter of an inch, which is not enough to move the gauge much but is the first rain on it since Sunday.
waters.note: No water temperature came back from the gauge this morning, so no warm-water trout line can be printed. The only NWS product active in West Virginia at 5:37 a.m. was a Special Weather Statement for heat in the lowland counties from Mason and Cabell to Kanawha and Braxton; Webster County is not on it. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, still carries the July 17 notice closing Forest Road 86-Williams River from July 20 for flood-damage repair, the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground bridge alert, the Sept. 8 Forest Road 76 closure and the Sept. 14 Forest Road 19 order on the Dolly Sods side; nothing is dated Sept. 15 or 16. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison on all three USGS gauges this morning reaches back to Monday 5:45 a.m., the first point of the two-day trace; its read string, 'prime wading water', is printed as written.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.62 feet, down 1.14 since Tuesday morning, flattening overnight.
waters.read: 24.6 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 1.14 from the 25.76 this paper printed at this hour Tuesday; the fetcher's 25.68 comparison is Monday morning's number, the first point of the two-day trace, and its falling flag agrees with the trace. The pool topped at 25.89 feet at 7:45 a.m. Tuesday, then fell all day: 25.59 at 11:45 a.m., 25.28 at 1:45 p.m., 25.13 at 3:45, 24.99 at 7:45 p.m., 24.78 at 11:45, 24.73 at 1:45 a.m., 24.66 at 3:45, a low of 24.58 at 4:45 and 24.62 at 5 a.m., so it dropped more than a foot in a day and has held within a tenth for the last three hours. The Weather Service's forecast for Point Pleasant, issued 10:12 a.m. Tuesday, had 25.2 at 8 a.m. today, 25.1 by 2 p.m., 25.0 Thursday and 24.8 by Sunday morning; the river is already half a foot under the whole curve, and action stage is 38 feet, so this is normal pool with Sunday's creek color gone. Shad, skipjack and crawfish are the forage, and wing dams, riprap, the lock wall and barge cuts the structure: with the pool pulled down a foot and flat, the shad are back on the current faces and the wing-dam tips in the little flow there is, so a white swimbait or a chartreuse-and-white spinnerbait across the upstream faces and off the tips, a black-and-blue jig with a crawfish trailer dragged down the riprap points where the drop is now a foot closer to the bank, and a walking topwater over the barge cuts in the fog before 9 a.m., which is the only cool water of the day. NWS Charleston's forecast for Point Pleasant has patchy fog before 9 a.m., sunny with a high near 92 and a heat index to 101, a southwest wind around 5, a slight chance of storms before 11 p.m. and a low around 70; a Special Weather Statement for heat covers Mason County until 3 p.m.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam; USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater. NWS Charleston's Special Weather Statement, issued 5:04 a.m. and running to 3 p.m., puts heat indices in the mid-90s to 100 across the lowland counties including Mason, Cabell, Jackson and Wood. The NWPS observation for POPW2 is 24.67 at 3 a.m., matching the USGS trace at that hour; the NWPS forecast page still carries the Tuesday-morning curve the river has already run under. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried again this morning and no lock notice is printed.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 27.33 feet, down 0.95 since Tuesday morning, off a 28.59 crest Tuesday afternoon.
waters.read: 27.3 ft and rising — up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Falling, not rising. Tuesday's paper had the river easing off a 28.50 crest Monday evening; it went back up once more, to 28.59 feet at 1:30 p.m. Tuesday, the top of the whole two-day trace, and has fallen since: 28.13 at 5:45 p.m., 27.97 at 7:45, 27.71 at 9:45, 27.60 at 11:45, 27.51 at 1:45 a.m., 27.32 at 3:45 and 27.33 at 5 a.m., a drop of a foot and a quarter in 15 and a half hours, with the last two hours holding in a 27.27-to-27.36 band. The fetcher's rising flag compares 27.33 against 27.0 at 5:45 a.m. Monday, the first point of the trace, and is wrong for today; the direction here is the trace's. Point Pleasant, 14 miles above the dam, fell 1.14 in the same 24 hours, so the fall is on both sides of the dam. The Weather Service's forecast for Huntington, issued 10:12 a.m. Tuesday, carries 27.2 at 8 a.m. today, 26.7 by 2 p.m., 26.5 by 8 p.m., 26.4 at 2 a.m. Thursday, 26.2 Thursday afternoon and 26.1 from Friday through Saturday; action stage is 48 feet. A foot and a half over the early-September pool and dropping, the river is between the read's two sentences: shad and skipjack are still pinned in the eddies below the lock wall and behind the wing dams this morning, so a three-quarter-ounce white swimbait or a skipjack-pattern jerkbait worked along the seam where the eddy meets the flow for hybrids and white bass, but as the stage comes off through the afternoon the current faces and the tips of the wing dams come back into play, and a crawfish-colored football jig dragged down the riprap where the color still hangs is the bank cast. Bank access is ordinary at 27.3. NWS Charleston's forecast for Huntington has patchy fog before 9 a.m., sunny with a high near 94 and a heat index to 102, a southwest wind around 5, a slight chance of storms before 11 p.m. and a low around 71; the heat statement covers Cabell County until 3 p.m.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's trend flag and read string say rising because they compare against Monday 5:45 a.m.; the observed trace since 1:30 p.m. Tuesday is a steady fall, so the read is printed as the fetcher wrote it with its flag dropped, and the direction here is the trace's, with the numbers the gauge's. The NWPS observation for HNTW2 at 5 a.m. is 27.41, eight-hundredths above the USGS figure, and the river at 5 a.m. was already under the 27.6 the NWPS forecast had for 2 a.m. NWS Charleston's Special Weather Statement for heat, issued 5:04 a.m., covers Cabell and Wayne counties until 3 p.m. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried again and no lock notice is printed.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 12:20 AM at 3.4 ft, low 6:29 AM at 0.8 ft, high 12:54 PM at 4.1 ft, low 7:20 PM at 1.2 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 5:05 AM at 0.7 ft, high 11:44 AM at 4.9 ft, low 6:11 PM at 1.1 ft, high 11:58 PM at 3.6 ft. Water 81.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. Moon waxing crescent, 22% lit, 4.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 12:20 AM and 12:54 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Spring tides easing toward neap: the moon is four and a half days past new and three days short of first quarter, and the sound swings 3.3 feet from the 6:29 a.m. low to the 12:54 p.m. high, two-tenths less than Tuesday, with 4.2 feet of range at the ocean station, so the inlet current is still hard but a little softer each day. The sound today runs 70 minutes behind the inlet on the midday high and 84 and 69 minutes behind on the two lows, so the flood in the backwater runs from 6:29 a.m. to 12:54 p.m. and the afternoon ebb from 12:54 to 7:20 p.m. First light falls on the 6:29 low, dead water at the inlet, but by 7 the flood is moving, and a topwater walked along the grass edges and over the oyster bars on the rising water is the dawn drum bite Native Son and Carolina Flats both described on Sept. 1; as the water tops the bars toward 1 p.m., a gold spoon or a paddletail on a quarter-ounce head in the flooded grass, and a live shrimp under a popping cork over the deeper oyster edges for the trout, which Speckled Specialist had scarce but big. The last of the ebb, roughly 5:15 to 7:20 p.m., is the red drum window on the tide preference that matters most here, shrimp and finger mullet draining out of the grass into the creek channels, and a cut mullet or a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig a couple of feet off the channel edge at a creek mouth; Spring Tide's over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches are release fish under footnote C. Flounder are catch-and-release: the Carolina Flats bucktail-and-Gulp setup along the ICWW channel edges and dock pilings stays a way to find them on the ebb, not a way to keep them. After dark the flood from 7:20 p.m. pushes bait past the dock lights, and a small paddletail or shrimp imitation drifted through the edge of the light is the trout cast. Surf: with a northeast wind around 10 and surf of 1 to 2 feet in the Weather Service's surf zone forecast, the calm-morning Spanish and bluefish pattern is closer than it was Tuesday's northeast 15, so a Gotcha plug or a metal jig under birds off the pier ends early is the cast; the strong north-to-south longshore current in the Beach Hazards Statement is the reason to stay on the pier and off the bar, and the piers' bottom fishing for black drum, Virginia mullet and pompano in the Sept. 1 report is the fallback.
waters.note: The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry September report is 15 days old, published Tuesday, Sept. 1, and the feed opened at 5:38 a.m. carries nothing newer; it is the month's pattern, not this morning's water. All four sound events fall inside today, midnight to midnight, and the fetcher tagged no spillover; the surf's 11:58 PM high is tonight, Wednesday. A Beach Hazards Statement issued by NWS Wilmington at 3:17 a.m. runs from 6 a.m. through this evening, to 8 p.m., for Coastal Pender and Coastal New Hanover, for a strong north-to-south longshore current and a moderate risk of rip currents. The surf zone forecast for Coastal Pender, issued 3:03 a.m., has a MODERATE rip current risk through this evening, surf 1 to 2 feet, no thunderstorm or waterspout potential, a high UV index, water around 80, sunny with a high in the lower 80s and northeast winds around 10, and gives the Topsail Inlet high as 11:44 a.m.; Thursday is a low rip risk with surf around 2 feet and northeast 5 going east, and Friday through Sunday are low. NWS Wilmington's point forecast for the island has sunny and 83 with a northeast wind of 8 to 12, clear and 66 tonight. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook has no active systems and one area, a trough about 600 miles east of Bermuda, at 10% in 48 hours and 30% in seven days, nothing near the Carolinas. Hampstead is the sound station and the tide that matters; the surf forecast's inlet high, 11:44 a.m., runs 70 minutes ahead of the sound today, not the 67 of Tuesday. Water temperature is Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, not the sound.

sections.note: All four waters reported from out/fishing.json, fetched 5:33 a.m. and not re-run. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison on every USGS gauge this morning is Monday 5:45 a.m., the first point of the two-day trace; the Williams and Point Pleasant falling flags agree with the traces, but Huntington's rising flag does not, the river having crested 28.59 feet at 1:30 p.m. Tuesday and fallen a foot and a quarter since, so its direction is printed from the trace. Point Pleasant dropped 1.14 feet in 24 hours and is already under the Weather Service's forecast curve; the Williams is at 72.9 cfs, 17 cfs over its pre-rain base. The only NWS product in West Virginia is a Special Weather Statement for heat indices to 100 in the lowland counties until 3 p.m.; a Beach Hazards Statement with a moderate rip risk and a strong longshore current covers Coastal Pender 6 a.m. to 8 p.m.

kicker: Kotozakura is the last unbeaten man at the Aki basho after Day 4; the Crew host Orlando City in the U.S. Open Cup semifinal at 7 p.m. ET, and the second Gauley release window opens Friday.
